entries.title: James 1:2
segments: Count it all joy. The true view of temptation or trial is that it is an opportunity to gain new strength through overcoming.

entries.title: James 1:3
segments: The proving of your faith worketh patience. Here proving has the sense of testing; and patience implies not a mere wilted submission, but the cheerful turning to good account of every untoward circumstance and event.

entries.title: James 1:4
segments: Perfect and entire. The work of patience is toward completeness, as expressed in a well-rounded character.

entries.title: James 1:5
segments: Wisdom. The wisdom here designated is the understanding of the things of God, as distinguished from that wisdom of the world which is foolishness with God (

).
 

 
 And upbraideth not. The text here expresses the great long-suffering of God whose giving must be limited by the degree of desire and willingness to accept on the part of those who ask.

entries.title: James 1:6
segments: Nothing doubting. Doubt, either as to the value of the gift or the power of the Giver, must weaken faith.

entries.title: James 1:9
segments: Glory in his high estate. The condition of freedom from the distractions of great possessions (
), becomes a high estate through singleness of heart and purpose.

entries.title: James 1:10
segments: And the rich, in that he is made low. The empty vessel is prepared to receive the larger blessing.

entries.title: James 1:11
segments: So also shall the rich man fade away in his goings. The idea of possession cannot endure longer than the riches upon which it is based, and which are here compared to the grass that withereth.  With the perception that his possessions are not enduring riches, the belief that he is a rich man fadeth away.

entries.title: James 1:12
segments: The crown of life. Life here is used in the same sense as in

: 'And this is life eternal, that they should know thee the only true God, and him whom thou didst send, even Jesus Christ.' The enduring of temptation advances the knowledge of God through the confirming of faith in His righteousness.

entries.title: James 1:13
segments:
A Servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ. The term servant is used not in any sense of servitude, but rather as expressing consecrated devotion, springing from the full acceptance of the gospel as the truth.
 

 
 Despersion. The body of the Jews then scattered throughout the Roman Empire.

entries.title: James 1:14
segments: Drawn away by his own lust. The word lust ahs here its wider significance, of all desire toward sense gratification as used in

: 'For all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh and the lust of the eyes and the vainglory of life, is not of the Father, but is of the world.  And the world passeth away and the lust thereof.'

entries.title: James 1:17
segments: The Father of lights. The source of all intelligence.

entries.title: James 1:18
segments: A kind of firstfruits of his creatures. In the old Jewish worship the firstfruits of the harvest were consecrated to God (
).  Being brought forth by the word of truth, we are the first of God's creatures to know ourselves His children and voluntarily to consecrate ourselves the firstfruits of understanding.

entries.title: James 1:25
segments: The law of liberty. This distinction is more clearly stated by Paul in
: 'For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus made me free from the law of sin and death.'
